title: Arrays and Indexed Data
summary: Store ordered values together, read items by position, and grow a collection with push.

sketchBlocks.title: An array gives many values one shared home
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
An **array** stores an ordered collection of values. Use one when several values belong together and their position matters.

```js
const eventNames = ["Welcome Fair", "Jazz Night", "Poetry Reading"];

console.log(eventNames[0]);
console.log(eventNames.length);
```

Line by line:

1. `eventNames` stores three strings inside one array.
2. `eventNames[0]` reads the first item. JavaScript array positions start at `0`.
3. `eventNames.length` reports how many items are in the array, so it produces `3`.

Indexes answer **where is this item?** while `length` answers **how many items are there?** Those are different questions, and keeping them separate prevents off-by-one mistakes.

quizDraft.title: Recognize array behavior
quizDraft.prompt: Which statements about arrays are true? Select all that apply.
quizDraft.hint: Separate position, count, and adding an item.

help.concept: Indexes, length, and push answer different array questions.
help.hint_1: One operation reads by position, one reports the collection size, and one changes the collection.
help.hint_2: Reject the statement that shifts the first position forward by one.

options: `items.length` reports how many items are stored.
`items.push(value)` appends a value to the end.

quizDraft.title: Read from a playlist
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: A playlist stores several song titles together, and the player needs to retrieve one specific track without creating a separate variable for every song. Task: Create `tracks` with three song titles. Create `secondTrack` from the second array item, then log `secondTrack` and the array length. Expected result: the Console shows the second title and a length of 3.
quizDraft.hint: Use the array position for the second item and keep the length check separate.

help.concept: Array indexing reads a value by position, while length reports the collection size.
help.hint_1: The array needs three text values before you read from it.
help.hint_2: Create `secondTrack` from the position immediately after the first index, then log it with `tracks.length`.
